findings.description: The docstring says the section is written 'if at least one is documented', but the condition requires every argument to have help. A command with one documented and one undocumented positional argument now gets no Positional arguments section at all.
findings.rationale: Trigger: a command with two Argument params, where only one has help=. The all() check is False, so the section is skipped entirely. Mechanism: the condition is all(...) rather than any(...), so the documented argument is hidden too. Impact: help output drops the positional arguments section for partially documented commands, which is the opposite of the stated intent to list every argument.

findings.description: When the command has no Argument params, all() over an empty list is True, so the 'Positional arguments' heading is emitted with no entries beneath it.
findings.rationale: Trigger: any command that has only options and no positional arguments, such as a plain flag-only command. The old code skipped the section when args was empty. The new code enters the with-block because all([]) is True, and formatter.section writes the heading before yielding, so an empty heading appears. Impact: every help page for a command without positional arguments shows a stray empty 'Positional arguments:' header, a visible regression on a common path.
